questions.q: Why do SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL each add a procedural layer on top of standard SQL?
options: Because plain declarative SQL (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) has no built-in way to express variables, loops, or branching logic
Because standard SQL doesn't support SELECT statements
Because procedural SQL runs faster than declarative SQL in every case
Because the ANSI SQL standard requires every vendor to add a procedural extension
questions.explain: Declarative SQL describes the result you want; procedural extensions add variables, control flow, and reusable routines that plain SQL statements can't express.

questions.q: What makes T-SQL different from the other three platforms' procedural languages structurally?
options: T-SQL's procedural logic (DECLARE, IF, etc.) can be used directly in any batch, with no enclosing procedure or block required
T-SQL requires every statement to be inside a stored procedure
T-SQL has no concept of variables at all
T-SQL cannot run SELECT statements inside procedural code
questions.explain: Unlike PL/SQL, MySQL stored programs, or PL/pgSQL, T-SQL lets you write DECLARE/IF/WHILE as a loose batch without wrapping it in a block or CREATE PROCEDURE.

questions.q: Which language's structure is described as closer in spirit to Ada than to T-SQL?
options: PL/SQL
MySQL stored programs
T-SQL itself
Standard ANSI SQL
questions.explain: PL/SQL's strict DECLARE-section-before-BEGIN, and its BEGIN/EXCEPTION/END structure, resemble Ada more than T-SQL's looser batch style.

questions.q: What is genuinely unusual about PostgreSQL compared to the other three platforms here?
options: PostgreSQL doesn't ship with one single fixed procedural language — it supports multiple pluggable PL languages, with PL/pgSQL as the default almost everyone uses
PostgreSQL has no procedural capability of any kind
PostgreSQL only allows procedural code inside triggers
PostgreSQL's procedural language cannot use variables
questions.explain: PostgreSQL supports PL/pgSQL, PL/Python, PL/Perl, and others as installable extensions, unlike the other three platforms which each have one fixed procedural language.

questions.q: How does this lesson characterize MySQL's stored-program language relative to T-SQL and PL/SQL?
options: Simpler and historically more limited, though it has genuinely improved across versions
More feature-rich than PL/SQL
Identical in every respect to T-SQL
Incapable of using IF or DECLARE under any circumstances
questions.explain: MySQL's procedural feature set has historically lagged behind T-SQL and PL/SQL (fewer functions, no packages, limited error handling), while still improving over time.
